auth.description: Mailchimp Marketing API key, granting whatever the account that issued it can do. Travels as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, the alternative Mailchimp documents beside its Basic form. The key's trailing `-us14`-style suffix names the account's datacentre; that value is asked for separately as configuration and is never read back out of this credential
auth.name: mailchimp.api_key
auth.subject: unstated

config.help: The short region code in front of `api.mailchimp.com` for your account, like us14 or us6. Find it three ways, whichever is easiest: it is the first part of the URL on your Mailchimp API keys page; it is the last part of your API key, after the final - character; or, on an OAuth connection, the OAuth metadata endpoint returns it. Enter the code alone, not a full URL
config.label: Mailchimp datacentre
config.name: server_prefix

config.help: Generate one under Account & billing, Extras, API keys in your Mailchimp account. It grants everything your Mailchimp user can do, so treat it as a password. Copy the datacentre code above from the same page before you leave it
config.label: Mailchimp API key
config.name: api_key

description: Mailchimp Marketing API: check connectivity, read audiences and their contacts, add or update a contact, and list campaigns. Authenticates with a single API key sent as a bearer token, against a host whose datacentre label the operator supplies

operations.description: Check that the API is reachable and the credential works. Takes no argument and returns no account data — Mailchimp calls it a health check that returns nothing account-specific. Also this connector's `verify`: it is the one call that proves both halves of the configuration at once, because a wrong key and a wrong datacentre label both fail it

health_status.description: Mailchimp's fixed cheerful string when everything is working. Its presence is the signal; its wording is not a contract and must not be matched on

operations.description: List the audiences in the account, with the id every contact operation takes. Returns Mailchimp's default first page only — this connector declares no paging parameters, so compare the number of entries against `total_items` before treating the result as complete

campaign_defaults.description: Default from-name, from-address, subject and language for campaigns sent to this audience. Left untyped rather than enumerated

contact.description: The physical mailing address printed in campaign footers, required by anti-spam law. Left untyped rather than enumerated

email_type_option.description: Whether contacts may choose plain-text or HTML

id.description: The audience id — what every operation below calls `list_id`

list_rating.description: Mailchimp's own 0-5 engagement rating for the audience

name.description: The audience name, as it reads in the UI

permission_reminder.description: The line Mailchimp prints in every campaign reminding a contact why they are receiving it

stats.description: Member counts and engagement averages. Left untyped rather than enumerated in full; `member_count` is the field most callers want

subscribe_url_short.description: The audience's hosted signup form — a link to give a human

visibility.description: `pub` or `prv` — whether the audience is listed publicly

web_id.description: The id in Mailchimp's own web UI, which is not the API id

total_items.description: How many audiences exist in total, which is how a caller sees that this page is a prefix

operations.description: Get one audience by id, with its settings and current member counts

params.description: The audience id, from mailchimp-audience-list's `id`. Not the `web_id` shown in Mailchimp's own UI

operations.description: List the contacts in an audience, subscribed and unsubscribed alike. Returns Mailchimp's default first page only — this connector declares no paging or status filter, so compare the number of entries against `total_items` before treating the result as complete. Every entry is personal data

members.description: The contacts on this page. Personal data: addresses, names and signup IPs

full_name.description: The contact's name, if the account collects one. Personal data

id.description: The MD5 hash of the lowercase email address — this is the `subscriber_hash` the contact operations take, so a caller that has read a contact never has to compute one

interests.description: Interest-group membership, keyed by group id. Left untyped rather than enumerated

ip_opt.description: The IP the contact confirmed opt-in from. Personal data

ip_signup.description: The IP the contact signed up from. Personal data; read it only if the flow genuinely needs it

last_changed.description: When this contact record last changed

list_id.description: The audience this contact belongs to

location.description: Approximate latitude, longitude and timezone. Left untyped rather than enumerated

member_rating.description: Mailchimp's 1-5 engagement rating for this contact

merge_fields.description: The account's own merge tags and their values — FNAME, LNAME and whatever else the operator configured. Account-defined, so left untyped rather than enumerated. Frequently personal data

stats.description: Open and click rates for this contact. Left untyped rather than enumerated

status.description: `subscribed`, `unsubscribed`, `cleaned`, `pending`, `transactional` or `archived`. `cleaned` means Mailchimp stopped sending after hard bounces

tags.description: The tags applied to this contact. Left untyped rather than enumerated

timestamp_opt.description: When the contact confirmed opt-in — the record that a double opt-in happened

unique_email_id.description: A stable id for the address across the account

web_id.description: The id in Mailchimp's own web UI

total_items.description: How many contacts the audience holds in total, which is how a caller sees that this page is a prefix

operations.description: Add a contact to an audience, or update the one already there. Creating with `status_if_new = "pending"` makes Mailchimp send its own opt-in confirmation and record the consent; creating with "subscribed" asserts that the account already holds that consent and sends nothing. Setting `status` on an existing contact changes whether they receive mail. This writes personal data about a third party and is not undone by calling it again

params.description: The MD5 hash of the contact's email address, lowercased first. It is NOT the email address. Compute it caller-side from the same address passed as `email_address`, or read it from mailchimp-audience-member-list, where it is each contact's `id`. A hash that does not match `email_address` addresses a different contact
params.name: subscriber_hash

params.description: The contact's email address. Must be the address `subscriber_hash` was computed from — Mailchimp addresses the record by the hash and takes this as the address to store
params.name: email_address

params.description: The status to give a contact this call creates; ignored when the contact already exists. "pending" makes Mailchimp send its own opt-in confirmation email and record the consent, and is the correct value unless the account already holds documented consent for this address; "subscribed" asserts that it does and sends nothing
params.name: status_if_new

params.description: The status to set on a contact that already exists. "unsubscribed" stops mail to them; "subscribed" resumes it and carries the same consent obligation as creating one. "cleaned" is Mailchimp's own marker for an address it gave up on and is not a value to set by hand
params.name: status

email_address.description: The contact's address as stored. Personal data

full_name.description: The contact's name, if the account collects one. Personal data

id.description: The MD5 hash of the lowercase email address — echo it back to confirm the call addressed the contact it meant to

interests.description: Interest-group membership, keyed by group id. Left untyped rather than enumerated

ip_opt.description: The IP the contact confirmed opt-in from. Personal data

ip_signup.description: The IP the contact signed up from. Personal data

last_changed.description: When this contact record last changed, which this call has just set

list_id.description: The audience the contact was written to

location.description: Approximate latitude, longitude and timezone. Left untyped rather than enumerated

merge_fields.description: The account's own merge tags and their values. Account-defined, so left untyped rather than enumerated

stats.description: Open and click rates for this contact. Left untyped rather than enumerated

status.description: The contact's status after this call — `pending` means Mailchimp has sent a confirmation and is waiting for the person to answer it, so the write is not yet a subscription

tags.description: The tags applied to this contact. Left untyped rather than enumerated

timestamp_opt.description: When the contact confirmed opt-in — the consent record this call may have just created

operations.description: List the campaigns in the account — drafts, scheduled, sending and sent alike. Returns Mailchimp's default first page only, and this connector declares no status or date filter, so compare the number of entries against `total_items` before treating the result as complete

archive_url.description: The campaign's public archive page — a link to give a human

content_type.description: How the campaign's content was authored — `template`, `html` or `multichannel`

emails_sent.description: How many emails this campaign has delivered so far

recipients.description: The audience and segment this campaign targets; `list_id` and `recipient_count` are the fields most callers want. Left untyped rather than enumerated in full

report_summary.description: Headline delivery statistics for a sent campaign — opens, clicks, unique rates. Absent on a campaign that has not been sent. Left untyped rather than enumerated

send_time.description: When it was sent, or absent if it has not been

settings.description: Subject line, title, from-name, reply-to and authoring options. Left untyped rather than enumerated in full

status.description: `save`, `paused`, `schedule`, `sending` or `sent` — a draft and a delivered campaign are told apart here

tracking.description: Which opens, clicks and third-party analytics this campaign records. Left untyped rather than enumerated

web_id.description: The id in Mailchimp's own web UI

total_items.description: How many campaigns exist in total, which is how a caller sees that this page is a prefix
